 Oral Judgment

In this appeal, the petitioner has challenged the judgment and award dated 21-12-2015 in M.V.C.No.298/2015 passed by the learned XII Additional Small Causes Judge and Member MACT,
Bangalore, (SCCH 8) ('the Tribunal' for short).

entities.text:
XII Additional Small Causes Judge and Member MACT,
Bangalore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the ranks of the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Undisputedly, there was an accident on 28-07-2014 at 5.30 p.m., involving TVS XL Moped bearing No.KA.02-EC-3318 and tempo 407 bearing No.KA-11-A- 2786 near Mahesh shop of Kodigehalli Village, Malavalli NC: 2024:KHC:37468 Taluk.
In the accident the petitioner as rider of the moped sustained the injuries.

After taking treatment at Government Hospital, Malavalli;
Mandya Institute of Medical and Teaching hospital, Mandya and at KIMS Hospital, Bangalore, the petitioner has approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation of Rs.25,00,000/-.

entities.text: Mandya Institute of Medical and Teaching hospital, Mandya
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.

After taking the evidence and hearing both parties, the Tribunal by impugned judgment awarded compensation of Rs.4,96,957/- with 8% interest p.a.
Pleading inadequacy and seeking enhancement, the petitioner is before this Court in appeal.

4. Heard the arguments of Sri Babu M, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri H.S.Lingaraj,
learned counsel for the Insurance Company.
5.

It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner that in the accident, petitioner has suffered multiple fracture of left femur, he was under hospitalization for 44 days at the above hospitals, injuries NC: 2024:KHC:37468 have affected his earning capacity as he was prevented from starting his own industry.

The Tribunal did not consider the income of the petitioner and that the percentage of disability taken by the Tribunal is on the lower side in spite of the evidence placed through PW2- Dr.Ravish V.N., Orthopedic Surgeon and sought for enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that the petitioner no-doubt has suffered the fracture of left femur, the injuries have explained in multiples.

PW2 is not the treated Doctor, he is only an assessing Doctor and the disability was assessed disproportionately,
the Tribunal awarded interest at 8% p.a., which is on the higher side and that the compensation awarded is proportionate to the nature of injuries suffered, avocation and income of the petitioner and it is not a case for enhancement.
I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of both the parties and perused the material on record.
8. The insurance company has admitted its liability to pay the compensation and has already satisfied the award passed by the Tribunal.
Hence, the point is only regarding quantum of compensation.
9. The medical evidence on record goes to show that the petitioner has suffered fracture of mid shaft of left femur, fracture of neck of left femur and fracture great tubercity of left humerus.
He was under hospitalization for a period of 44 days.
The petitioner has been provided with physiotherapy and this has been explained by PW3- Dr.Sudin Maharjan, Physiotherapist.
The expenses incurred by the petitioner along with the bills have been placed before the Tribunal which are amounting to Rs.2,11,997/- and the same is ordered to be reimbursed to the petitioner.
PW2-Dr. Ravish V.N., Orthopedic Surgeon KIMS has assessed the disability of the petitioner to the extent of 20.66% to the whole body, whereas, the Tribunal has taken at 13%.

The petitioner is aged 49 years and he was working as a Superintendent at Bhagavan Buddha Homeopathy Medical College and Hospital, Bangalore, prior to accident, he has left the job to open his own manufacturing unit for production of Paper Plates and Cups.

entities.text: Bhagavan Buddha Homeopathy Medical College and Hospital, Bangalore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: On the date of the accident, the petitioner was an ex-employee of Bhagavan Buddha Homeopathy Medical College and Hospital and his evidence did not point out the pension that he has received anything on the date of the accident.

entities.text: Bhagavan Buddha Homeopathy Medical College and Hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Exhibits P.17 to P.19 are the documents pertaining to the application filed by the petitioner for grant of industrial Unit.
The petitioner is yet to start the business and therefore, there is no proof of income at the time of accident.
In the year 2014, a person with no proof of income, would be earning not less than Rs.8,500/- per month and the same is to be applied for the case on hand.
The medical evidence thus speaks of 20.66% to whole body disability having regard to the fracture of left femur, it is proper to assess the functional disability of the petitioner at 15%.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.60,000/- towards pain and sufferings, Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities and discomforts and Rs.15,000/- towards future medical expenses.
The same is kept in tact.
The petitioner will be laid up for a minimum of six months, having regard to 44 days of Mr K M Kumaraswamy vs Cholamandalam Ms General Insurance ...

3 hospitalization, the loss of income during the laid up period for six months comes to 8,500x6 =
Rs.51,000/-.

The incidental expenses spent by the petitioner towards attendant charges,
conveyance, food and nourishment is to be awarded at Rs.30,000/-.
Loss of future income will be 8,500/-x 12 x 13 x 15% =1,98,900/-.
The total compensation comes to Rs.6,06,897/- as against Rs.4,96,957/- and thereby enhancement of Rs.1,09,940/- which is rounded off to Rs.1,10,000/-.
It is the just compensation that the petitioner is entitled to, in the facts and circumstances of the case.
As regarding rate of interest is concerned, the Tribunal has awarded 8% interest per annum.
Tribunal did not point out any reason for awarding interest at 8% p.a.
Since the insurance Company is not in appeal and it is not proper to meddle with the discretion of the Tribunal.
But insofar as enhanced compensation is concerned, the petitioner has to be awarded interest at 6% per annum.
Hence, the appeal merits consideration.

iv) The Insurance Company shall deposit enhanced compensation with interest supra NC: 2024:KHC:37468 from the date of petition till the date of deposit within eight weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of the judgment.

SD/-
(T.G. SHIVASHANKARE GOWDA) JUDGE tsn*
